newsitem.title: BELGIUM: First euro-denominated bond listed in Luxembourg.
newsitem.headline: First euro-denominated bond listed in Luxembourg.

text.p: The first bond denominated in euro, issued by the European Investment Bank, was listed on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange on Friday.

"The listing of the bond on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange... confirms the close and long relationships established between the Luxembourg Stock Exchange and the European Investment Bank," a statement from the exchange said.
The 1.0 billion Ecu-into-euro April 2004 bond, with a 5.25 percent coupon, was announced in late January. Until the introduction of the euro, planned for 1999, the notes will be paid for in Ecu.
Technically, the euro becomes the 40th listing currency to be used in the Luxembourg market, the statement said.
About 8,500 international bonds issued by a range of private, public, sovereign and supranational issuers are listed on the exchange.

The exchange believed it would in the future remain the reference centre for the listing of international securities "thanks to the modern infrastructure...and to the excellent and frequent contacts which it maintains with professionals, both in Luxembourg and abroad."
